said: log that: our Instagram post about the spring sale got almost no likes because we posted it at 11pm. I expected the usual 40 or so likes.
log that: the newsletter subject line that asked a question got twice the opens of our usual 'Monthly update' line. I expected the same open rate as always.
log that: we had to redo the website banner because the brand colours on it were from the old logo. I expected the designer to have the new brand file.
log that: a lead went cold because nobody followed up for nine days after the first call. I expected a follow-up within two days.
log that: sending the quote as a one-page summary with the detail attached got a yes the same day. I expected the usual back and forth over a long PDF.
log that: I quoted a kitchen job without checking the site and had to re-quote when we found the wall was load-bearing. I expected the photos to be enough.
log that: a customer complained that nobody told them the installer would be a day late. I expected the office to call them.
log that: sending new customers a short welcome video cut the 'how do I log in' emails to almost nothing. I expected the written guide to be enough.
log that: we had to redo the onboarding checklist for new clients because it skipped the contract signature step. I expected the old checklist to cover it.
log that: we picked the new accounting software on a demo alone and found out a month later it can't do multi-currency. I expected the demo to show what we needed.
log that: writing down three options with costs before the team meeting meant the decision took ten minutes instead of an hour. I expected the usual long debate.
log that: we chose to open a second location because one month was busy, and that month turned out to be a one-off. I expected the trend to hold.
log that: the crew showed up before the materials because the delivery was booked for the wrong day. I expected the supplier's confirmation to match the schedule.
log that: we redid the weekly schedule because two jobs needed the same van. I expected the shared calendar to catch it.
log that: batching all the small repair jobs on Tuesdays saved us about a day of driving each week. I expected it to make no difference.
log that: an invoice went out with last year's tax rate and we had to reissue it. I expected the template to have the new rate.
log that: we paid a supplier twice because the invoice came by email and by post. I expected the system to flag the duplicate.
log that: reconciling the bank every Monday morning meant month-end took one day instead of three. I expected it to feel like extra work.
log that: the new hire spent her first two days with no laptop because nobody ordered it. I expected IT to know she was starting.
log that: giving the contractor a recorded walkthrough instead of a written brief got the job right first time. I expected a few rounds of questions.
log that: I had to redo a task I delegated because I never said when it was due. I expected it back by Friday.
log that: the spreadsheet total was wrong because the SUM formula stopped two rows short after we added rows. I expected the total to update.
log that: the agent deleted the test file I asked it to fix. I expected it to change one function.
log that: asking the agent to write the tests first meant the new booking form worked first time. I expected the usual two rounds of bug fixes.
log that: the chatbot summary of the supplier contract missed the auto-renewal clause. I expected it to list every date and deadline.
log that: giving the chatbot two of my old emails as examples made its drafts sound like me. I expected generic drafts.
log that: I had to redo the AI's blog draft because it invented a customer quote. I expected it to use only the notes I gave it.
log that: the office move went faster once every box had a number that matched the floor plan. I expected the usual mix-ups.
log that: the charity event raffle ran out of tickets in the first hour because we printed 100. I expected about 100 people.
log that: we had to repaint the shop sign because the council needed a permit we didn't know about. I expected a sign repaint to need no permit.
log that: the price on our website and the price in the quote didn't match, and the customer noticed before we did. I expected them to be the same.
log that: a customer who had already paid was sent our sales follow-up sequence asking if they were ready to buy. I expected paid customers to be removed from it.
log that: we chose the delivery company with the lowest price and two parcels arrived broken. I expected the same care as before.
log that: the chatbot wrote a formula for the commission sheet that rounded every amount down. I expected exact amounts.
log that: I asked the team in the group chat to update the price list and nobody did it because nobody knew it was theirs. I expected someone to pick it up.
